records.deidentified_narrative: u1 was in a hit and run accident prior to this crash;the driver that struck his vehicle fled. this report can be found under sapd18231691. u1 was traveling [roadway]. u1 was attempting to catch up to the hit and run driver and obtain a license plate. u1 driver said that his tire did not feel right after the initial accident, he believed that it was hitting something. u1 lost control of his vehicle as the pavement was slick, his speed exceeded the posted speed limit, and his tire was possibly damaged. u1 spun out and crashed into both u2 and u3, both units were parked and unoccupied. u4, u5, and u6 were on foot and were working on u2; u4 was under the vehicle. u5 and u6 were between u2 and u3. u1 crashed into the vehicle they were working on, which caused u2 to fall off the jack it was on. u4 was crushed under the vehicle, u5 and u6 were between the vehicles and were thrown. u4 suffered serious injuries according to ems, u5 suffered minor injuries, [medical facility]; neither had life threatening injuries. u6 suffered minor injuries, he was treated onscene. contributing factor's are u1's speeding (over limit) and possible defective brakes and left rear wheel (wheel was bent as a result of the first crash). det stated that u1 did not apply his brakes before the accident. sgt. almanza #3066 was notified and made the scene. det davis #2406 of tid was at the scene. csi knudson #9408 processed the crash site.

units 1 and 2 both moved to the right on the roadway. unit 1 left the roadway and collided front concentrated to a wooden utility pole located on the side of the roadway. unit 1 also sustained left distributed damage after becoming entangled in wiring that was attached to the pole. the driver of unit 2 stated she observed unit 1 approaching. she knew from the distance between the vehicles that she had time to turn. she stated she turned and then realized that unit 1 was driving over the speed limit. she decided to try [roadway] to get out of the path of unit 1. she stated unit 1 moved with her, to the right, and left the roadway. she then observed unit 1 hit the utility pole. the driver of unit 1 stated she was going about 40mph. she stated unit 2 turned in front of her vehicle. she moved to the right to avoid unit 2. unit 2 moved to the right with her. she left the roadway and hit the utility pole. unit 4, a pedestrian, parked her vehicle at the location and walked to the driver of unit 1. it is believed she is a witness to the crash or stopped to assist. her vehicle was not involved in the crash. witness aubrey duenas [phone] stopped also. ---------- the crash was reported to dallas 911. dallas police and fire responded to the crash scene. dallas fire rescue ambulance #28 arrived at the crash scene at 1:17pm. dfr paramedics david gilmore and john mueller exited the ambulance and observed the driver of unit 1, unit 4, and witness duenas, on foot, near downed power and utility lines. the paramedics called for them to walk towards them away from the lines. the paramedics walked to them, and then began walking with them, away from the lines. unit 3 [roadway] [roadway]. the driver of unit 3 stated he was driving slowly with the hazard lights on. the utility pole that unit 1 hit broke in two places and dropped to a lower height. the pole was broken but the paramedics stated it was still in a vertical position. there were [roadway] that were now much lower than they should have been if the pole had not been hit. unit 3 hit [roadway] with the top of the vehicle. the lines became hung on the enclosed box of the vehicle. unit 3 pulled the broken section of utility pole down. the pole fell on top of unit 4 knocking unit 4 to the roadway. investigating officer observed that unit 1 drove through the utility pole, breaking the pole in two places, and was not at rest against it. investigating officer submitted a request for a search warrant to vehicle crimes unit detective c clark #6712. the warrant was to obtain the airbag control module from unit 1. senior corporal m phillips #6654 executed the search warrant and obtained the pre-crash data for unit 1. unit 1 was going 63mph 4 to 5 seconds out, 65mph 2 to 3 seconds out, 50mph 1 second out, and 46 mph at impact. the driver of unit 1 applied the [case id] 2. 5 seconds out. the antilock brake system activated 2 seconds out. unit 1 was speeding over the posted speed limit. the speed of unit 1 denied the driver of unit 2 the ability to yield the right of way. if the driver of unit 1 would have been driving at or near the speed limit then unit 2 could have safely turned and the crash would not have occurred. unit 3 contributing factor 98-other; insufficient overhead clearance. witness tracy trice [phone] witnessed the utility pole being pulled down by unit 3. detectives c clark #6712 and g baum #7698 responded to the crash scene from the vehicle crimes unit. nfi.

records.public_safe_text: police responded to the listed location for a woman walking along the right shoulder and then an accident call. upon arrival i contacted the people involved in an accident who stated that a woman, listed at unit 2, was hit on the roadway. unit 2 was deceased so i called for tid to make the scene. i spoke to the people involved in the accident. i spoke to (d1 of unit 1) and he stated that he [roadway] and he saw an 18 wheeler start [roadway]. (d1) started to slow a little bit not knowing what the truck was doing. (d1) stated that he then saw a female, unit 2, [roadway] towards the right side of the roadway. (d1) started applying his breaks and started skidding. (d1) stated that his vehicle struck unit 2 with the front right corner. unit 2 flew into the air and struck the right side of his windshield. (d1)'s vehicle came to [roadway] and he exited the vehicle to see if he could pull unit 2 out of the roadway. (d1) stated that he got there too late and the female was struck by another vehicle, unit 5. i spoke to (d3 of unit 3) and she stated that she was coming up behind (unit 1) and saw the [roadway] and she was unable to avoid (unit 1) and struck the vehicle in the left rear and the left door which was open still from when (d1) exited. (d3) stated that her car bounced off of (unit 1) and struck (unit 4). the driver of (unit 4) stayed in the left shoulder after she was hit. i spoke to (d4) later and she stated the same that she was passing the [roadway] when she was struck by (unit 3). (d5 of unit 5) called in after striking [roadway]. other officers contacted (d5) and got his information for the report. safd arrived on scene and burrier #850 pronounced the pedestrian deceased at 0530. sgt w smith #3301 arrived on scene and he was informed of all needed information. we called for a csi to make the scene. tid arrived on the scene and j goodwin #2322 started to process the scene and got all the information he needed from me and the drivers. crime scene investigator e roberson #9431 processed the scene. crime scene investigator j valadez #9442 processed unit 5 and took photos of unit 5. the medical examiner k freveletti #122 made the scene and conducted her investigation and took pictures of the body and the scene. the contract ambulance took the pedestrian to the medical examiners office to see if they could identify the female. unit 3 and unit 4 were unable to be driven. they were both towed by mission towing to locations of the drivers choice. all the other vehicles were able to be driven from the scene. coban and bwc are both available.

records.deidentified_narrative: unit 1 was stopped to proceeded through the dale/frey intersection, which is controlled by a 4-way stop sign. unit 1 then travelled north through the intersection. as unit 1 entered the crosswalk area, unit 2 and unit 3 were running east down the sidewalk. unit 2 and unit 3 ran out into the intersection at full speed without slowing for vehicles already in the roadway. unit 1 stated he never saw unit 2 or 3 until about the time of the collision. unit 2 and 3 stated they didn’t see unit 1 until about the time of the collision. unit 2 collided with the left front quater panel of unit 1 just behind the tire. since unit 1 was traveling north, the driver’s side mirror then collided with the right side of unit 2’s head/face, causing unit 2 to fall to the ground. unit 3 observed unit 1 at the last moment, and stopped prior to fully colliding with unit 1, however the outside portion of unit 3’s elbow collided with an unknown portion of unit 1. unit 1 came to a stop quickly after the collision. unit 2 sustained various non-incapacitating injuries to his head, left shoulder, left wrist, and various scrapes [medical facility] by his mother. unit 3 sustained a scrap to her right elbow, and denied treatment at the scene. unit 1 sustained only minor damage to the driver’s side mirror, as the mirror popped out of the bracket upon the collision with unit 2. a witness to the incident stated unit 1 didn’t appear to be traveling recklessly, and unit 2 and unit 3 appeared to be in a full run as they ran out into the intersection from the sidewalk without slowing.

[date] / 1200 hrsi received this incomplete crash report for follow up investigation, based on the information provided by the initial responding officers i found there to be workable evidence. [date] / 1300 hrsi conducted a follow up at a beer depot located at [roadway], el paso county texas. i spoke to the owner jose jimenez (dob [date]) and asked if his security cameras might have captured the incident on video. [person] yes he did in fact capture the incident, and further had already saved the video because he thought that someone from our department might be coming by to ask for it. [person] the video for me and saved it for me [roadway]. after observing the incident very clearly on his tv monitor, i determined that a white color ford dually was traveling westbound at the 100 block of talbot when the deputy collided with the left rear portion of the vehicle as he was engaged in a foot pursuit with a suspect. the deputy was traveling on foot west then cut north when he collided with the pickup truck. after the deputy collides with the pickup he spins round then continues with is foot pursuit. at the time of the collision the vehicle slows down, then continues [roadway]. at no time did the pickup truck collide with the deputy involved, nor did the deputy fall to the surface of the roadway from being struck by the pickup. after reviewing the video footage several times, i determined that the driver of the vehicle was not at fault in this collision, and that the impact from the deputy to the pickup truck was only minor. a copy of the video footage was uploaded into this report under attachments. this crash report will reflect complete, and the i-leads report will reflect closed cleared. deputy giovanni segoviano #2153traffic / sti

mcdonalds located on summer crossing. she stated she was walking to her vehicle and was standing near it when unit 1 began backing out of a parking spot. she stated the back left area of the vehicle struck her on her left leg and hip area. she stated she began hitting unit 1 with her hand to alert the driver she was there and that an older b/f rolled her window down and told her she had not seen her. smith did not tell the driver of unit 1 that she was hurt and did not call 911. she stated she followed unit 1 after the driver left and took a picture of the lpn and then drove to bi-state to report the incident. she stated her left leg [medical facility]. i asked her why she didn't call police right then, but she stated just decided to come to bi-state to file the report. she stated she spoke to her co-workers inside [medical facility] and that she could file the report at bi-state. she also stated that she was trying to find the non emergency number to the police department when the driver of unit 1 left the scene. i was able to take the lpn, ar 237ukp, from the photo she took of unit 1 and locate the driver and the owner. i made contact with the owner and driver by phone. the driver of unit 1 stated her back up camera did not show anyone in her view. she stated she heard the female hitting her vehicle and apologized for not seeing her. she stated the passenger was on the side of the vehicle. she denied hitting the female with her car and stated that the female never told her she had been hit. her information was obtained by phone. i tried to obtain video of the incident from mcdonalds, but was informed the manager that had access to the video would not be available until monday. unit 1 owner: kamilah golston [phone], unit 1 driver: angela murphy [phone], pedestrian: jaquonza smith, [phone]
